_source: HYG Database v3.0 (astronexus.com) + Gaia DR3 (2022) + HIPPARCOS (1997)
_note: Stars within 30 light-years. Positions are J2000.0 equatorial coordinates.
_coordinate_system: Visualization XZ-plane is galactic plane (approx). Y is perpendicular to disk.

stars.name: Sol
stars.note: G-type main sequence star. Will become red giant in ~5 Gyr.

stars.name: Proxima Centauri
stars.note: Nearest star. Has confirmed planets: Proxima b (habitable zone), c, d. Frequent stellar flares make habitability uncertain.

stars.name: Alpha Centauri A
stars.note: Binary with α Cen B. Third-brightest star system in sky. Near-solar twin.

stars.name: Alpha Centauri B
stars.note: K-type companion to α Cen A. Binary period ~80 years. Separation 11–36 AU.

stars.name: Barnard's Star
stars.note: Highest proper motion of any star (10.3 arcsec/yr). Will be nearest star in ~10,000 years.

stars.name: Wolf 359
stars.note: Famous as site of Borg battle in Star Trek: TNG 'The Best of Both Worlds' (1990). Named in episode for real star.

stars.name: Sirius A
stars.note: Brightest star in the night sky (magnitude -1.46). Binary with Sirius B (white dwarf). Worshipped by ancient Egyptians — heliacal rising marked Nile flood.

stars.name: Sirius B
stars.note: White dwarf — dead stellar remnant of a former ~2 M_☉ star. Now the size of Earth, mass of the Sun. First white dwarf discovered (1862).

stars.name: Epsilon Eridani
stars.note: Confirmed planet: ε Eri b (Jupiter-mass, a=3.4 AU). Prominent debris disk. Early SETI target (Project Ozma, 1960).

stars.name: Tau Ceti
stars.note: 5 planet candidates including e and f in habitable zone. Featured in many science fiction works. SETI target.

stars.name: 40 Eridani A
stars.note: Gene Roddenberry + astronomers identified this as Spock's home star system in 1991 letter to Sky & Telescope. Third member of triple star system.

stars.name: Altair
stars.note: Rotates so fast (9h period) it is significantly oblate — 20% wider at equator than poles. Directly imaged by interferometry (Monnier et al. 2007).

stars.name: Vega
stars.note: Standard star for photometric magnitude calibration (magnitude 0 by definition). Will be the North Star in ~13,000 years due to precession. Has debris disk.

stars.name: Fomalhaut
stars.note: Prominent debris ring imaged by HST (Kalas et al. 2005). Planet candidate Fomalhaut b may actually be an expanding dust cloud from collision.
